_comment: Per-keyword translation context. When a source string contains any of these keywords (word-boundary, case-insensitive), the matched hint is attached to the AI prompt's <source> element as a `hint="..."` attribute. Unlike glossary.json (which forces a fixed target rendering), context entries provide CONCEPT-level disambiguation so the model picks the correct sense of an ambiguous word in any target language. Keep hints locale-agnostic: describe what the word means inside TranslatePress's UI, not how to render it in a specific language. Per-locale overrides can live in bin/translations/context-{locale}.json if a specific locale genuinely needs tighter steering; the per-locale file is merged on top of this default. Multiple matched hints on the same source are joined with ' | '.
string: In TranslatePress, 'string' refers to a piece of translatable text — a chunk of human-readable text the plugin extracts from the website so it can be translated. Use the target language's standard term for a UI/text segment in this sense; do NOT use the 'rope/cord' meaning.
strings: Plural of 'string' in the translatable-text sense — pieces of translatable text the plugin manages. Same guidance as 'string': UI/text segments, not ropes/cords.
regular: In the String Translation interface, 'regular' qualifies user-input strings, as opposed to gettext strings defined by developers. Translate in the sense of 'plain / general / ordinary text strings entered by the user', not 'periodic / scheduled / recurring'.
slug: URL slug — the URL-friendly identifier portion of a web address (e.g. the 'my-page' in /my-page/). Keep as 'slug' if the target language has no established equivalent, otherwise use the locale's standard term for a URL identifier. Do NOT use the animal/lazy-person meaning.
slugs: Plural of URL slug — URL-friendly identifiers for pages/posts. Same guidance as 'slug'.
post: WordPress post — a piece of published content / article on the website. Use the target language's standard word for a blog article or piece of content. Do NOT use the mail/postal meaning, nor the verb 'to post (something somewhere)'.
posts: Plural of WordPress post — published articles/pieces of content. Same guidance as 'post'.
advanced: 'Advanced' often appears as a Settings tab label or section heading where the implicit noun is 'Settings/Options' (the user is already inside a settings interface). When the source is the bare word 'Advanced' with no noun next to it, render it the way the locale would naturally label such a tab — typically an adjective agreeing with the implicit noun 'settings/options' (often plural or neuter as the grammar requires). Do NOT leave it as a dangling adjective with no implicit noun, and do NOT translate it as the adverb 'additionally / extra / more' — it modifies 'settings', not 'in addition'.
